coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Power Station Park
record.summary: Planned ~1.2-acre central park in two blocks either side of Maryland Street: East between Blocks 8 and 12 (multi-purpose lawn and plaza opening to Unit 3 and the Stack) and West between Blocks 7 and 11 (play plaza). Schematic design was approved by the Planning Director on June 23, 2022 (Case 2017-011878PHA-03). A Phase 1 open space delivered with Blocks 8 (East) and 11 (West); as of the March 2025 annual report neither block nor the park was under construction. Financing of $200 million for the Block 8 residential building, which delivers the park's east half, was reported on Aug 3, 2026 (the Chronicle says the building 'would rise', so construction has not started); the amended development agreement, which includes Phasing Plan amendments, passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, and its effect on the park's timing has not been read.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- the outline is built from recorded Assessor lot lines except one cut. West part (between Blocks 7 and 11): the east arm of lot 4232011. The two lots 4232011 and 4232012 are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams: Louisiana Paseo is the north-south strip made of lot 4232012 and the west strip of lot 4232011, and Power Station Park West is the east-west arm of lot 4232011. The line between them, about 33 m long through lot 4232011, is not a recorded lot line: it is the straight extension of the strip's east edge, which the recorded vertices of both lots lie on to within 0.1 m. East part (between Blocks 8 and 12): all of lot 4232013, a recorded lot, with no cut. No document names the lot as the park; it is matched by location to the D4D's Power Station Park East. The park is planned and not yet built.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn): the east arm of lot 4232011 (recorded 2022-08-30; active), cut from the rest of that lot along a straight line, and all of lot 4232013 (recorded 2022-08-30; active). Cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 4.25.1 - Power Station Park and Louisiana Paseo: Concept Plan Overview (printed p.119), which labels the two park areas 'Power Station Park West' (2) and 'Power Station Park East' (1), and Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The park is two areas on two sets of lots: the west part is the east arm of Assessor lot 4232011 (assigned from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams; its west edge is a straight extension, not a recorded lot line) and the east part is all of lot 4232013. Both lots are active, recorded 2022-08-30. No document names either lot as the park.
notes.regulatory_context: The site's central public open space, per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label -- two rectangles, one between Blocks 7 and 11 (labelled 'POWER STATION PARK') and one between Blocks 8 and 12, on either side of Maryland Street; Block 9 lies east of Delaware Street and does not border it. Not yet built: consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) and the SF Chronicle of Aug 3, 2026 (Block 8 construction 'expected to begin in the fall'). Of the blocks around it, Block 7B (the Sophie Maxwell Building) sits 'between Humboldt Street, Maryland Street, Louisiana Paseo and Power Station Park' (2024 annual compliance report) and opened in October 2025 (SF YIMBY, Oct 24, 2025); the others are still planned.

changes.text: The park is now described as the Design for Development draws it: two plain rectangles on either side of Maryland Street, not an irregular shape, with Block 9 not bordering it; an earlier dated note in the map's history that called it one rectangle was corrected. The expected completion moved from 2028 (a press figure) to 2029, the end of Phase 1's schedule in the October 2020 approval, and the note that Block 8 was still seeking financing was corrected: the Chronicle (Aug 2026) says JPMorgan agreed to finance about $200 million and construction is expected to begin in the fall. The design review approval of 8.3.21 is no longer attributed to staff, the note that the blocks around the park are still planned was removed (Block 7B has opened), the dead 2019 draft link was replaced with the final February 2020 document, and the land-use figure is tagged as a document rather than a rendering.

open_questions: No construction start, groundbreaking or completion date for either park block was found in any source through 2026-09-17; the park is tied to Blocks 8 and 11, and the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) says Block 8 construction is 'expected to begin in the fall' after JPMorgan agreed to finance about $200 million. The map shape's 'not yet built' note is consistent with the March 2025 annual report but nothing later confirms it. The expected-completion milestone uses Phase 1's overall schedule (2020-2029 in the October 2020 approval), not a park-specific date.
No cost figure for Power Station Park was found (annual reports give contract values only for streets, Unit 3, Sophie Maxwell, Station A).

Landscape architect identification rests on the 'plural' logo and 2724 17th Street address on the 7.29.21 plan sheets plus CMG's 'Affiliated Landscape Architect: Plural Studio'; no document names the firm in text; the Design for Development credits CMG Landscape Architecture on its open-space figures.
Annual reports 2021-2023 print the design review submittal date as '3.23.20'; the Planning staff memo says March 23, 2021. The memo date is used.

The 2021 annual report lists Power Station Park East as 'Design review approved, 8.3.21' delivered with Block 12; from 2022 it is listed as delivered with Block 8 with a site permit application. The reason for the change is not stated.

Phase 1 application table (Table 5) lists Power Station Park West as moved from DA Phase 2 to Phase 1; the East block does not appear in that change table (presumably already Phase 1) - not confirmed against DA Exhibit M.

BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated DA) passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary (Resolution No. 21945) describes the proposed Phasing Plan changes to park delivery: now 'Power Station Park East must be provided with Block 12' and 'West must be provided with Block 11'; proposed 'East may be provided with either Block 8 or 12' and 'West ... with either Block 7 or 11'. The final text sent to the Mayor was not read.

Whether the Phase 1 Street Improvement Project was completed: the 2024 annual report expected Q4 2025, and the Port Commission staff memo of Nov 14, 2025 says the developer 'anticipates receiving a Notice of Completion in the first quarter of 2026' (an expected date); no later source confirms completion. The start is given as both April 2023 and June 2023 within the 2024 report; DataSF shows the permit filed 2023-04-03 and issued 2023-06-23.

Area of Power Station Park, by source: about 1.2 acres, two blocks (D4D 4.1); ~1.2-acre (SF Planning); 1.22 acres (DEIR); approximately 1.26 acres (Phase 1 application). The IMP gives 1.92 acres under the combined heading 'Power Station Park and Louisiana Paseo' (the text calls it a 'proposed 1.92-acre central green space' and names the paseo separately, so whether the figure includes the paseo is not stated), and the pre-application slides give '2 acres' for park plus paseo.
